angle_name: Mollified explicit formula: M_K(s) = Σ_{d≤K} μ(d)d^{-s} as an unconditional mollifier at zeta zeros, with Landau–Gonek dilational μ-correlations
mechanism: The bilinear object μ * dR (R = π − Li) has Dirichlet series (P(s) − L(s))/ζ(s), P the prime zeta function, L the Mellin transform of dLi; the log(1/(s−1)) singularities of P and L cancel exactly at s = 1, so the series is log((s−1)ζ(s))/ζ(s) up to tame terms and its only singularities are zeta zeros. Truncation to d ≤ K replaces 1/ζ(s) by the Dirichlet polynomial M_K(s), which is precisely the classical mollifier of ζ. Step 1: replace R(⌊x/d⌋) by R(x/d) (cost ≪ K ≪ √x since each floor changes R by O(1)), and transfer π − Li to ψ − t by partial summation (log-factor losses only). Step 2: apply the truncated explicit formula ψ(t) − t = −Σ_{|γ|≤T} t^ρ/ρ + O(t log²(xT)/T) inside the d-sum, giving S ≈ −Σ_{|γ|≤T} (x^ρ/ρ) M_K(ρ) + remainder; x stays pinned, all structure moves to the spectral side. Step 3 (per-zero bound, unconditional): partial summation of M_K against m(u) = Σ_{d≤u} μ(d)/d ≪ exp(−c(log u)^{3/5−ε}) (Vinogradov–Korobov for μ) gives |M_K(ρ)| ≪ (1+|γ|)(1−β)^{−1} K^{1−β} exp(−c(log K)^{3/5−ε}), so with K ≍ √x each zero contributes ≪ x^{1−(1−β)/2} exp(−c′(log x)^{3/5−ε})/(1−β): the μ-side and Λ-side zero-free-region savings ADD instead of taking a max. Step 4 (the lens's distinctive leverage, for pushing beyond): the discrete second moment Σ_{|γ|≤T} |M_K(ρ)|² recombines via Landau/Gonek's formula Σ_γ n^{iγ} ≈ −(T/2π)Λ(n)·(n-power corrections) into dilational μ-correlations Σ_e μ(e)μ(ke)Λ(k)(·), and dilational (multiplicative-shift) correlations — unlike additive Chowla shifts — are EXACTLY computable by multiplicativity: μ(e)μ(pe) = −μ(e)²·1_{p∤e}, forcing a systematic negative sign that is the visible source of the empirical flat cancellation coefficient. Honest ceiling: reassembling the pinned zero-sum from the moment needs Cauchy–Schwarz over zeros, whose x^{2β} spread reproduces the pointwise-ψ wall; unconditional output of this angle is therefore PNT-shape with a strictly better constant (rung 0+, beating the trivial triangle bound by a full extra exponential factor), and rung 2 through this lens alone is equivalent to controlling M_K at hypothetical low-lying off-line zeros, i.e., RH-adjacent. The zero-sum ↔ prime-sum toggle is an involution; I state that plainly rather than disguise it.
new_leverage: Two items, both UNVERIFIED as to novelty. (a) Additive stacking of zero-free-region savings: the per-zero bound x^β|M_K(ρ)| ≪ x^{1−(1−β)/2}·exp(−c(log x)^{3/5−ε}) multiplies the VK savings of the μ-side polynomial into every zero's contribution, including zeros at the zero-free-region boundary — the trivial triangle bound gets only one savings factor; this gives an unconditional bound with a strictly larger exponential constant than either side alone. (b) Dilational μ-correlations in the Landau–Gonek discrete moment are exactly computable by multiplicativity (μ(e)μ(ke) with k a prime power factors, sign −1), keeping the μ×R sign interaction alive through the recombination — structurally unavailable to any additive-shift (Chowla-type) or Mertens-square approach. Risk: (b) may be implicit in the classical mollifier literature (Conrey–Ghosh, Gonek, Levinson); I cannot verify from the packet.
target_estimate: Named estimate "Mollified zero-sum bound": for x ≥ x₀, y = ⌊√x⌋, K = ⌊x/(y+1)⌋, T = exp(θ(log x)^{3/5}) with θ optimized: (i) representation Σ_{d≤K} μ(d)(ψ(x/d) − x/d) = −Σ_{|γ|≤T} (x^ρ/ρ) M_K(ρ) + O(x (log x)³/T + √x log x), where ρ = β+iγ runs over nontrivial zeros; (ii) per-zero bound |M_K(ρ)| ≤ C(1+|γ|)(1−β)^{−1} K^{1−β} exp(−c(log K)^{3/5−ε}) valid unconditionally for all zeros with (1−β) ≥ (log K)^{−2/5}; (iii) conclusion |Σ_{d≤K} μ(d) R(⌊x/d⌋)| ≪ x exp(−c*(log x)^{3/5−ε}) with c* strictly exceeding the constant obtainable from the triangle inequality plus pointwise VK on R alone (the gain is additive: c* ≈ c_μ + c₀/(2θ^{2/3}) capped by Perron truncation θ). Losses along the way: O(√x) from floor removal, log-power losses in the ψ→π−Li transfer, log³x in Perron, and the (1−β)^{−1} ≤ (log T)^{2/3} factor per zero absorbed into ε.

obstacle_positions.F_closure: Exits the declared class: the only Mertens-type input is m(u) = Σ_{d≤u}μ(d)/d with VK savings (not Σ M(d)² ≪ D^{1+2σ}), and recombination over d is the explicit formula evaluated at zeta zeros (harmonic analysis on the spectral dual), not Cauchy–Schwarz/Hölder/triangle over d. The sign interaction survives as M_K(ρ) evaluated with signs at each zero, and in the moment variant as exactly-computed μ(e)μ(ke)Λ(k) correlations. Honest flag: the Cauchy–Schwarz-over-ZEROS step in the moment variant suffers an ANALOGOUS expansion (x^{2β} spread across off-line zeros) — not literally in 𝔉, but the same disease in dual coordinates; the rung-0 version avoids it entirely by bounding per-zero with signs discarded only after the mollifier savings is extracted.
obstacle_positions.fiber_growth: Not engaged: there is no pair-(d,d′,a,a′)→modulus transfer anywhere; the frequency set is the fixed spectrum of zeta zeros, independent of d, so no fibers and no conductor aggregation. This obstacle is avoided by construction, not solved.
obstacle_positions.pinned_vs_averaged: x remains pinned throughout; all averaging is over the spectral dual (zeros up to T), which is legitimate for a single pinned x — no exceptional-set risk from x-averaging. Residual exposure: Landau's formula at pinned integer arguments resurrects Λ(n)-terms at n = ratios d/e; these are explicit and finite, handled term by term. The arithmetic synchronization of x enters only through which Λ(d/e) terms are hit — visible, not hidden.
obstacle_positions.modulus_magnitude: Avoided: no wheel modulus appears; the analytic conductor is the Perron height T = exp(θ(log x)^{3/5}) (or x^ε in conditional variants), vastly below any wheel modulus; no √(full-modulus) claim is made or needed.
obstacle_positions.parity: The mechanism is not sieve-theoretic; μ enters linearly paired against Λ-weights via ζ and Landau's formula, so the classical sieve parity wall is not directly engaged. Position stated plainly: the parity-type hardness reappears in equivalent form as the possibility of low-lying off-line zeros where M_K cannot be shown small; this angle trades the parity wall for the zero-location wall — no free lunch is claimed.
obstacle_positions.circularity: Fully confessed and structurally central: the zero-sum ↔ prime-sum duality is an involution, so a conditional-on-RH bound of the zero-sum is the self-consistency direction and worth nothing for promotion. The d = 1 term R(x) is never bounded pointwise; it is absorbed into the same explicit formula and controlled only by the unconditional zero-free region. All claimed unconditional content is confined to the VK region plus the mollifier partial-summation bound — no RH-strength pointwise prime bound is used anywhere.
obstacle_positions.finite_range: The flat empirical coefficient 0.35–0.43 is exactly what a zero-sum dominated by the first few zeros with roughly constant |M_K(ρ₁)/ρ₁| predicts, so the numerics are consistent with this mechanism but promote nothing; the same numerics were consistent with Mertens-conjecture-style deception. The kill test below deliberately probes whether the zero-sum needs inter-zero cancellation (deception-prone) or only per-zero smallness (robust).

kill_test: Cheapest kill (a day of compute, no theory): for x ∈ {10⁷, 10⁸, 10⁹}, K = ⌊x/(⌊√x⌋+1)⌋, compute M_K(ρ_j) at the first ~10⁴ zeros (β = 1/2, known numerically) and compare −Σ_j 2Re(x^{ρ_j} M_K(ρ_j)/ρ_j) against the directly computed Abel sum. Two kill conditions: (1) if the truncated zero-sum fails to converge to the Abel sum with a tail decaying in T, the representation loses too much in the remainder and the angle dies at rung 0; (2) if matching the observed |S| ≈ 0.10–0.18·√x requires massive cancellation BETWEEN zeros (i.e., Σ_j |M_K(ρ_j)| x^{1/2}/|ρ_j| overshoots by a large growing factor), then every absolute-value-based recombination (per-zero bounds, Cauchy–Schwarz over zeros, second moments) is provably insufficient for rung 2 and only signed evaluation survives — killing the moment-method upgrade path cheaply. Secondary micro-test: numerically verify the claimed partial-summation bound |M_K(ρ)| ≪ (1+|γ|)(1−β)^{−1}K^{1−β}exp(−c(log K)^{3/5}) at low zeros before writing the rung-0 proof.
rung0_plan: Unconditional, classical, ~10–20 pages, formalizable-shaped: (a) floor removal: |R(⌊x/d⌋) − R(x/d)| ≤ 2, total cost O(K) = O(√x); (b) transfer π − Li to ψ − t by partial summation (log-power losses); (c) truncated Perron/Riemann–von Mangoldt with T = exp(θ(log x)^{3/5}), remainder O(x log³x/T); (d) per-zero bound via partial summation of M_K against m(u) = Σ_{d≤u}μ(d)/d with the unconditional bound m(u) ≪ exp(−c(log u)^{3/5−ε}); (e) x^β ≤ x·exp(−c₀ log x/(log T)^{2/3}) from the Vinogradov–Korobov zero-free region; (f) optimize θ. Output: |Σ_{d≤K} μ(d)R(⌊x/d⌋)| ≪ x exp(−c*(log x)^{3/5−ε}) with c* strictly larger than the constant from the triangle inequality with pointwise VK on R (the honest trivial bound at this scale), because the μ-side and Λ-side savings add. This is a genuine PNT-strength unconditional bound on the Abel sum that demonstrably uses the μ×R interaction (steps d–e), qualifying as a rung-0 entrant that beats the trivial scale by an explicit extra exponential factor.
plausible_partial: Named partial, provable at bounded effort: "Additive stacking of zero-free-region savings for the mollified Abel sum" — the rung-0 estimate above, i.e., an unconditional bound x·exp(−c*(log x)^{3/5−ε}) on the Abel sum whose savings constant c* provably exceeds by a fixed factor the best constant obtainable from triangle inequality + pointwise VK on R, together with the exact evaluation lemma for dilational μ-correlations Σ_{e≤E} μ(e)μ(ke) = (multiplicative local factor)·Σ_{e≤E,(e,k)=1} μ(e)² + error for squarefull-free k — the latter a small standalone lemma of independent use to any future moment computation over zeros. Both are classical-analysis deliverables with no RH input.
self_assessed_risk: Weakest assumption, stated plainly: that the per-zero partial-summation bound on M_K(ρ) retains the full VK savings uniformly in the height and β ranges needed, without the (1+|γ|)(1−β)^{−1} factors or the ψ→π transfer swallowing the added constant — plausible but unchecked in detail. Broader risks: HIGH probability (my estimate ~70%) the angle caps permanently at rung 0+ — the pointwise-ψ analogy says zero-density estimates cannot push a pinned-x zero-sum below x^{1−o(1)} unconditionally, and the M_K factor only helps polynomially at off-line zeros while the wall lives at low-height zeros near σ = 1 where K^{1−β} is a loss, not a gain; MODERATE risk the dilational-correlation leverage is already implicit in the mollifier literature (Conrey–Ghosh, Gonek, Levinson) and hence not new; every capability claim here is UNVERIFIED speculation as required. Rung 2 through this lens alone is RH-adjacent by construction; I do not claim a path to it, only the sharpest unconditional extraction the lens permits plus a kill test that decides cheaply whether the moment-based upgrade path is worth anyone's time.
